clue.text: Book starts to question usual attitudes regarding the old

indicators.note: the starts of the six words that follow are taken, one initial letter from each in turn

explanation.surface: A volume that sets out to challenge conventional attitudes towards the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the first letter of each of the six words that follow, which spells the answer straight off.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarto is a book size made by folding sheets twice into four leaves, so it names a book.

clue.text: Forcing university to start revolution

indicators.note: the university's letter is put at the beginning of the other piece

parts.note: prising (open) means forcing

explanation.surface: Pressure on a university to launch a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a rebellion against authority, a revolt.

clue.text: Determined to produce notes on instrument

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits above, so before, another

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
so (soh) is another note of the sol-fa scale
the lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Resolved to play some notes on a lute.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolute means firm and steadfast in purpose.

clue.text: Accompaniment disturbed Gobbi a lot

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The opera singer Tito Gobbi was upset by the backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tito Gobbi was a celebrated Italian baritone, which suits the musical answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An obbligato is an instrumental part accompanying a solo voice.

clue.text: I don't believe you live in harmony

definitions.meaning: '... with you!' is a colloquial exclamation of disbelief
to coexist amicably, to be on good terms

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an informal cry of disbelief and a verb for being on friendly terms with someone.

clue.text: Follow current trend

parts.note: read literally it is drifting with a flow of water; figuratively it is conforming to what everyone else is doing

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to conform to prevailing opinion, like a boat carried along by water.

clue.text: Complain about a rule to the Speaker

indicators.note: what a listener hears is meant, so the phrase is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: reign means rule, and with 'a' sounds like the entry

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a regulation to the presiding officer of the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Speaker' looks like the Commons official, but it only signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to accuse or call to account, finding fault formally.

clue.text: Reformed a region's regiment

indicators.note: reformed means made again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A regional regiment has been reconstituted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regiment' looks like a noun but is the verb: to organise strictly.
explanation.definitionFit: To regiment is to impose strict order and organisation.

clue.text: Section of theatre put up heartfelt valediction

parts.note: the gods are the highest gallery in a theatre

indicators.note: in a down answer, put up means written bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: deep feelings are heartfelt ones

explanation.surface: From the theatre gallery comes a sincere farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Godspeed is a wish for a safe journey said on parting, a farewell.

clue.text: Rower seated on thwart — this could give rise to quarrels

definitions.text: this could give rise to quarrels

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece sitting on another comes after it

parts.note: to cross someone is to thwart them
bow is the rower nearest the front of a boat

explanation.surface: An oarsman sits on the cross-bench of a rowing boat, and arguments may follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thwart' looks like the boat's bench a rower sits on, but here it is a verb, cross. Quarrels are not arguments but the square-headed bolts fired by a crossbow.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is the short heavy bolt a crossbow shoots, so the weapon gives rise to them.

clue.text: Primarily, frozen stiff

indicators.note: 'primarily' means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: stiff and rigid are synonyms

explanation.surface: First and foremost, someone is chilled to the bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid means intensely cold, which is what being frozen stiff amounts to.

clue.text: Fortune-teller has succeeded in. portraying David

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the fortune-teller, so 'in' signals a container

parts.note: a palmist tells fortunes by reading hands
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant has managed to impersonate someone called David.
explanation.walkthrough: King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms, so he is the psalmist par excellence.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical tradition names King David as the author of most of the Psalms, making him the archetypal composer of sacred songs.

clue.text: Illegally take man, perhaps, in juvenile game

parts.note: a kid is a child, a juvenile
nap (napoleon) is a card game

explanation.surface: Snatching a person is part of a youngsters' game.
explanation.walkthrough: NAP, short for napoleon, is a trick-taking card game once popular in Britain. 'man, perhaps' marks a person as one example of what may be abducted.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to seize a person unlawfully, and a man is one example of a victim.

clue.text: Leaflet — one about physiotherapists' practice

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet
the Roman numeral I is one
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A pamphlet describing what physiotherapists do.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction, pulling on a limb to relieve pressure, is a treatment used in physiotherapy.

clue.text: Pearls may be controlled

definitions.meaning: pearls are commonly threaded together on a cord
like a puppet, wholly manipulated by someone

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase describes threaded beads; figuratively it means manipulated like a marionette.

clue.text: Monster conger eel oddly depleted

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are removed, so the even ones remain

explanation.surface: A fearsome conger eel that has strangely shrunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly depleted' strips the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of CONGER EEL, leaving the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, a classic monster.

clue.text: Exactly where girl's marriage prospects could depend

definitions.text: where girl's marriage prospects could depend
definitions.meaning: dot is French for a dowry, which marriage prospects might hang on

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means punctually; read literally with French dot, a dowry, it is what a bride's prospects rest on.

clue.text: Rare slip could produce such an aggressive response

indicators.note: the letters given could produce a new word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A rare blunder might provoke a hostile retaliation.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of retaliation against an enemy.

clue.text: Interpret the sound made by wind instrument

indicators.note: what is heard of the instrument's name, not its spelling, gives the entry

parts.note: a reed is a woodwind instrument or the vibrating part of one

explanation.surface: Explaining the note produced by a clarinet or oboe.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a situation or text is to interpret it.

clue.text: Salvage most of River Tees wreck

indicators.note: wreck means smash up, so the letters are thrown into a new order
most of a word means all but its last letter

explanation.surface: Salvaging the remains of a shipwreck on the River Tees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of Tees; 'wreck' then rearranges RIVER plus TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrieve something is to recover or rescue it, as salvage does.

clue.text: Lent is well on

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means lent money

explanation.definitionFit: Advanced means both paid out as a loan and well forward in progress.

clue.text: Chap with passion for publicity

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man, a chap
rage can mean a passion or craze

explanation.surface: A man with a fervent desire for the limelight.
explanation.definitionFit: Media coverage is the attention a story gets, which is publicity.

clue.text: To hold on,'to hold on — that's duplication

indicators.note: the first piece holds the next word inside it, so a container

parts.note: to cling is to hold on

explanation.surface: Clinging on and on again, which is just repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloning makes an identical copy, so it is duplication.

clue.text: School in distress

definitions.meaning: A famous English public school in north-west London

explanation.surface: A pupil suffers misery at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow is a well-known English boarding school; as a verb it means to cause acute distress.

clue.text: Trade Union to get money from Iran for instruction

parts.note: the rial is Iran's currency

explanation.surface: A union negotiates Iranian funding for a teaching programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a session of teaching for a small group, so it is instruction.

clue.text: Could I still, if only in part, concentrate?

indicators.note: only a part of the words is used, so the entry lies inside them

explanation.surface: A distiller wonders whether a partial setup could still reduce something.
explanation.walkthrough: The entry runs from the end of 'Could' through 'I' into 'still'.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilling a liquid removes water and concentrates it.

clue.text: Show extreme dislike in statements made in court

indicators.note: the extreme letters go inside the synonym for show, so 'in' signals a container

parts.note: evince means show, display

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Displaying strong hostility in what is said to a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extreme' takes DE, the first and last letters of 'dislike', which go into EVINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony given by witnesses in court is evidence.

clue.text: Woman informally allowed to return message

indicators.note: return means go back, so both pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: Marge is a familiar short form of Margaret
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A woman, casually permitted to send a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns MARGELET round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a message sent by telegraph.

clue.text: Piggish king eyed askance

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's cipher

indicators.note: askance means awry or sideways, so the letters are set crooked into a new order

explanation.surface: A gluttonous monarch is looked at suspiciously.
explanation.walkthrough: GR stands for Georgius Rex, the royal cipher of King George, so it is a standard crossword king.
explanation.definitionFit: Piggish behaviour is gluttonous, grabbing more than one's share.
